video_title: Hawks vs. Pistons Postgame Press Conference: Corey Kispert

quotes.speaker: Corey Kispert
quotes.summary_phrase: Corey Kispert on the importance of rebounding against the Pistons
quotes.excerpt: plays like that allow us more chances to score and then it deflates the other team.
quotes.quote: The most important thing. Lou tore it up, Zubi tore it up, Dyson tore it up on the glass. Plays like that allow us more chances to score and then it deflates the other team. We talk about that all the time as a group, emphasizing that kind of stuff. When you are on the other end and there is rebound after rebound after rebound and a big three, that flattens the other team. Credit to those guys for getting on the glass and cleaning it up. Seven offensive rebounds for Dyson, six for Jaylen, three for Lou, two for Zubi, that stuff goes a long way.
quotes.social_post: Corey Kispert credits the Hawks bench for their dominance on the glass against Detroit, noting that rebound after rebound and a big three really flattens the other team.

structured.context: Corey Kispert discusses the importance of rebounding and praises his teammates for their performance on the glass against the Pistons.

quotes.speaker: Corey Kispert
quotes.summary_phrase: Corey Kispert on the team's connected mindset and bench performance
quotes.excerpt: we try to come in and change the game and then hand it back.
quotes.quote: That is just the mindset that we have going into each game. Either we turn the game around or we carry what the starters have already started, and either way that does not affect what we do. We try to come in and change the game and then hand it back. Nights like tonight really help us carry that on and carry that forward. We are a super connected group, especially on that bench, and it shows through on the TV for sure.
quotes.social_post: Corey Kispert on the Hawks bench unit: We are a super connected group and it shows through on the TV for sure.

structured.context: Corey Kispert describes the mindset of the bench unit and the team's overall chemistry.

quotes.speaker: Corey Kispert
quotes.summary_phrase: Corey Kispert on refining his driving and shooting skills
quotes.excerpt: being able to read whether to drive it, whether to shoot it, or pass it and move it.
quotes.quote: For me, that is the skill. That is what has made me an NBA player. Either shoot it or drive it. Obviously, shooting it has been my main thing, that is my main skill, that is my NBA-level skill. But it is really easy to guard somebody that cannot drive as well. So, being able to read whether to drive it, whether to shoot it, or pass it and move it, that is the skill that I have had to get really good at over the course of my career to stick around. When you can do both and finish at the rim and also shoot threes at a really high level, you become really, really hard to guard.
quotes.social_post: Corey Kispert on his development as a scorer: It is really easy to guard somebody that cannot drive as well. When you can do both and finish at the rim and also shoot threes at a high level, you become really hard to guard.

structured.context: Corey Kispert explains his approach to developing his offensive game by balancing shooting and driving.

quotes.speaker: Corey Kispert
quotes.summary_phrase: Corey Kispert on maintaining consistency despite inconsistent playing time
quotes.excerpt: the only thing that I can control is how I approach it.
quotes.quote: I envisioned the consistency and envisioned the shooting for sure. And more than that, it is just a mindset thing. You guys have followed us the whole year, there have been long stretches where I have not played at all, and then there are games where I played and then not played. So with the inconsistency of minutes and not really knowing from game to game where I might stand, the only thing that I can control is how I approach it. Whether that is coming off the bench in games like this or cleaning up the last four or five minutes of a game altogether, I have to be ready to play because that is the job that I signed up for and that is the job that you have as an NBA player, just to play.
quotes.social_post: Corey Kispert on handling inconsistent minutes this season: The only thing that I can control is how I approach it. I have to be ready to play because that is the job that I signed up for.

structured.context: Corey Kispert discusses how he maintains a professional mindset despite inconsistent playing time throughout the season.

quotes.speaker: Corey Kispert
quotes.summary_phrase: Corey Kispert on finding open shots off offensive rebounds
quotes.excerpt: the way that you get threes against a really good defensive team like Detroit is off offensive rebounds.
quotes.quote: The way that you get threes against a really good defensive team like Detroit is off offensive rebounds. It is really hard for them to track the ball, track it off the rim, and then go find me, Aaron, whoever, to go guard them. That is where you can get your most open looks. It is something about the ball coming to you from the basket, it makes it easier to shoot it because it is like practice, versus having to catch it coming sideways off of a pick-and-roll or off the dribble. It feels more like practice when you get it off of an offensive rebound and shoot. Statistically, those are the ones that go in the most, those are the highest value threes that we can get, so you definitely want to hunt them and shoot them when you get those chances.
quotes.social_post: Corey Kispert explains why threes off offensive rebounds are the highest value shots: It feels more like practice when you get it off of an offensive rebound and shoot.

structured.context: Corey Kispert explains why offensive rebounds create high-quality three-point shooting opportunities against the Pistons defense.
